pages.text: Run into a mould, pig iron is cast iron, and it casts where steel will not: at four per cent carbon it melts nearly 400 °C lower than pure iron and runs thin into every corner of the mould.
pages.title: Cast iron

pages.text: In grey iron the carbon comes out as flakes of graphite, which make it machine cleanly and damp vibration and make it weak in tension: good for pipes, cylinders, frames, flywheels and machine beds, bad for anything that has to bend.
The Factory Must Grow's casting basin casts 144 mB of pig iron to a cast iron ingot, and its cast iron pipes, tanks, frames, flywheels and blast furnace come from that.
Before there is a blast furnace a little is made by hand: an iron ingot and a coal compacted in a heated basin, the iron taking up the carbon as it would in the hearth.
